newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia stocks easier at close on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Australia stocks easier at close on profit-taking.

text.p: The Australian share market closed a touch lower on Thursday as profit-takers sold into early gains after the benchmark All Ordinaries index pushed past the 2,500 mark.
The All Ordinaries closed at 2742.9, down 3.0 points on the day after touching a record intra-day high of 2,757.9, up on the previous high on Wednesday of 2,751.4.
"It's a little bit of profit-taking," said Robert Cameron of Cameron Securities. "We've had some pretty solid performances recently."
The All Industrials index ended in positive territory, buoyed by a good performance among retailers, while the resources sector was dragged down by gold.
Brokers said retail stocks may have been aided by Wednesday's economic data showing a rise in May retail sales.
Coles Myer Ltd, David Jones Ltd and Woolworths were all firmer, indicating a redirection of funds into perceived cyclical stocks, with building materials also firmer, brokers said.
Gold prices slipped to new four year lows offshore, accelerating the recent slide in the gold index, which fell 2.56 percent on the day.
Among the worst hit were Delta Gold, Newcrest Mining and Resolute Samantha, which all declined more than five percent.

In major resource stocks, the Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd peaked above A$20 (US$15) but sank back to close down 15 cents at A$19.68, while Rio Tinto dropped 57 cents to A$22.40 after a fall in London trading.
Elsewhere, Queensland Cotton gained 30 cents to A$5.80 after announcing the US$43 million purchase on Wednesdsay of the U.S.-based Anderson Clayton cotton processing group.
Jewellery retailer Angus & Coote slipped 20 cents to A$2.75 after saying it expected to see a minimal year profit.
